provenance.what: Ninth live run: both golden sets under grounding policy g3, which makes an answer's own list numbering structure rather than figures. Motivated by a field transcript on a real corpus: 'what are the step by step activities we should cover?' came back as a correct, fully cited three-item list and was refused for the figure 3 - the third item's own marker. The first two markers had passed only by coincidence, matching a locator (p. 1) and a heading (4.2). The collision was self-inflicted: prompt rule 6 asks the model to enumerate what the sources list, in their order, so the gate was rejecting the exact shape the prompt requests - and every steps, activities or priorities question paid for a frontier call before being refused. Markers are stripped only at line start and capped at two digits, so a line opening with a year stays audited and any figure an item claims is checked exactly as before.
provenance.models: Chat: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M via llama-cpp-python. Embeddings: nomic-embed-text v1.5 Q4_K_M, task prefixes applied.
provenance.corpus: evals/corpus/aveline in full (11 documents); companion run on the repository documents/
provenance.hardware: 4-core CPU container, no GPU; both model servers local
provenance.caveat: The local model on these corpora rarely answers in numbered lists, so this run proves g3 does no harm - the do-no-harm bar every gate change must clear. The behaviour it fixes was measured in the field on a frontier rung and is pinned by four unit tests, including the two that prove the gate keeps its teeth: a figure invented inside a numbered item is still refused, and a line opening with a year is still audited.
